replies.author: eliz0x
replies.text:
Map apps require sensors to function properly when using navigation (in a car, walking etc) so they know which direction you're facing etc. Also fitness/health apps to track steps.

Sensors being allowed by default is just a case that phones required them to be added into the hardware and then no work was done to restrict access.

Android was and still is a privacy nightmare. It had a lot of issues in the early days that have since been rectified but sensor limitation isn't one of them. So GrapheneOS has implemented it.

As for why you would want to limit it.. well apps can try to fingerprint you, track whether you walk or drive a lot, visit gyms etc which all combined could be used to build a profile of your daily activities.

I believe it is also known that apps can use fluctuations in the sensors to pick up words that are said close to the device.

For me, I have it blocked for all apps by default. Many will request access but nothing bad has come from not allowing it. Only ones I've allowed are map apps.
